macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise as technology shares lead
items.summary: The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq moved higher Monday as technology stocks rallied ahead of the third-quarter earnings season. Investors continued weighing elevated Treasury yields and expectations for Federal Reserve policy.[1]

items.title: Weak jobs data reduces expectations for October Fed hike
items.summary: September U.S. payroll growth was reported at just 29,000, well below expectations, while unemployment rose to 4.2%. The soft labor data has led markets to reduce expectations for another Federal Reserve rate increase this month.[3][10]

items.title: Fed meeting minutes become central market focus
items.summary: Investors are awaiting Wednesday’s release of minutes from the Federal Reserve’s September meeting for clues about the outlook for interest rates. Rising long-term Treasury yields and uncertainty over future policy remain key market drivers.[2][9]

items.title: Treasury yields and oil prices pressure global markets
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield remained above 5.3%, while crude oil prices stayed elevated amid geopolitical risks involving commercial shipping and the Strait of Hormuz. European markets were mixed, with France’s CAC 40 lower while Germany’s DAX and Britain’s FTSE 100 gained.[7][8]

items.title: C.H. Robinson agrees to acquire RXO
items.summary: RXO shares jumped more than 20% before the open after C.H. Robinson Worldwide announced a cash-and-stock acquisition valued at approximately $5.8 billion.[8]

items.title: Light earnings calendar shifts attention to upcoming reports
items.summary: The week’s major scheduled earnings reports include Constellation Brands, Levi Strauss, PepsiCo and Delta Air Lines, while investors also monitor technology-sector momentum and forthcoming corporate guidance.[2][9]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs above $86,000 as crypto market capitalization reaches $3.01 trillion
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 2.1% over 24 hours to $86,436, while the global cryptocurrency market cap increased 0.8% to $3.01 trillion. Ethereum gained 1.4%, BNB 2.2%, XRP 2.1%, and Solana 0.9% during the same period.[1]

items.title: CFTC proposes new framework for crypto-market oversight
items.summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission opened proposed rulemaking initiatives covering crypto-asset transactions and markets after the failure of the Clarity Act. The agency is seeking public feedback on the proposed framework.[2][10]

items.title: OKX and ICE venture seeks approval for tokenized U.S. stock trading
items.summary: OKXICE, a joint venture between OKX and Intercontinental Exchange, reportedly applied to the SEC to launch a tokenized U.S. stock-trading platform. The initial proposal would cover tokenized versions of 63 NYSE-listed companies and require full shareholder rights.[1]

items.title: Cardano rallies about 10% on upgrade and institutional-credit optimism
items.summary: ADA rose roughly 10% in 24 hours to more than $0.27, outperforming Bitcoin and Ether. Market attention focused on Cardano’s RealFi institutional-credit product and expectations surrounding the planned Dijkstra scalability upgrade.[7]

items.title: Zcash activates faster-block upgrade on public testnet
items.summary: Zcash’s NU7 upgrade, which targets 25-second blocks, went live on the public testnet ahead of schedule. The project is targeting a mainnet release in November.[3]

items.title: Bitcoin liquidations approach $52 million amid volatility
items.summary: Bitcoin’s price volatility generated approximately $51.996 million in BTC liquidations over the previous 24 hours as the cryptocurrency moved above $86,000. The Fear & Greed Index was reported at 70, indicating elevated market optimism.[9]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Sony reportedly considering revivals of classic PlayStation franchises
items.summary: New reports suggest Sony may be exploring revivals of Ape Escape, Killzone, and Sly Cooper, though the projects remain unconfirmed.[2]

items.title: Hellblade developer reportedly begins shedding staff
items.summary: Ninja Theory is reportedly reducing its workforce months after revealing a new project at an Xbox showcase, raising uncertainty about the game’s future.[7]

items.title: Epic Games CEO warns of severe traditional games-industry crisis
items.summary: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney reportedly said the traditional games industry is approaching a major downturn, comparing current conditions with the 1980s video-game crash.[1]

items.title: New details emerge on PUBG Studios’ Escape from Tarkov rival
items.summary: Financial-report information has reportedly revealed additional details about PUBG Studios’ unannounced extraction-shooter project.[4]

items.title: This week’s notable game releases include Gears of War: E-Day and Kingdom Hearts Collection
items.summary: The week’s release slate reportedly includes Gears of War: E-Day, Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen, Kingdom Hearts Collection [I-III], and other titles across major platforms.[6]

items.title: Dynasty Warriors remasters may continue
items.summary: Producer Tomohiko Sho reportedly said additional Dynasty Warriors remasters are possible, while expressing a preference for developing new games and sequels.[3]

items.title: Ubisoft reportedly expanding its generative-AI initiative
items.summary: A report claims Ubisoft’s Motherbrain generative-AI program is being treated as a company-wide initiative for game ideation, while Capcom is taking a more cautious approach.[8]
